verdict.rationale: Make ships a first-party MCP server that lets AI systems such as Claude and ChatGPT run scenarios and manage account contents, including viewing and modifying scenarios, connections, webhooks and data stores. It also provides Make Skills to help assistants build scenarios, so natural-language operation is possible. However, it works only through an external AI client, and the evidence shows no native in-product natural-language command interface. Missing for 10: a native in-app natural-language command surface, evidence of scenario building or editing from plain-language prompts inside Make, and hands-on or independent corroboration of how reliable natural-language operation is.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
View and modify scenarios and their related entities (e.g., connections, webhooks, and data stores)

Make Skills are Markdown files that help your assistant reliably perform Make-specific tasks, including building scenarios, configuring modules, and connecting to Make MCP server or third-party services.
